data.one_liner: Run Large Language Models on-device using Google's LiteRT-LM runtime.
data.what_it_does: A Flutter plugin providing local on-device inference for Large Language Models using Google's LiteRT-LM runtime. It supports hardware acceleration via CPU, GPU (OpenCL), and NPU, offering streaming chat, multi-turn conversations, multimodal inputs, and tool calling without network dependencies.
use_when: You need offline LLM execution in your app.
Prompts and data must remain strictly on-device for privacy.
You want to avoid per-token API costs and rate limits.
avoid_when: Your target devices have insufficient RAM to load large model files.
You require cloud-scale models that cannot fit on mobile hardware.
strengths: Fully offline execution with no API keys or token billing
Hardware acceleration via CPU, GPU (OpenCL), and NPU
Supports streaming responses, multimodal inputs, and tool calling
weaknesses: High memory usage can lead to out-of-memory crashes on large models
iOS requires a lengthy one-time local Bazel build process
iOS runtime currently limited to CPU backend only
data.setup_notes: Requires downloading large model files (.litertlm) and setting up writable storage paths. iOS builds require installing Bazelisk and running a manual framework build script that takes 30-60 minutes on first run.

alternatives.name: llamadart
alternatives.why_pick_it: Alternative on-device LLM solution if you prefer llama.cpp integration.

alternatives.name: firebase_ai
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you prefer cloud-hosted Gemini models instead of running models locally.
